info.title: Merges
info.description: TestSchema_Golden merges, into the property a of each case, every schema of its prefixItems in turn, failing with x-error where it has one, and drops the merged ones: the document must then be after.json. The components without properties a are what the cases refer to. Edit both by hand.

enum-takes-the-example.description: An empty enum takes the value of an example merged into it.

enum-of-integers-takes-the-example.description: So does an enum of another type than string.

enum-keeps-its-values-once.description: A value already in the enum is not added again.

first-example-and-description-stay.description: a keeps its own description and example.

a.description: The archived status of the page.

plain-string-and-uri.description: A string seen as text and as a URI.

null-and-null.description: Null merged with null stays null.

nullable-is-kept.description: a that may be null still may.

nullable-is-adopted.description: b that may be null makes a so.

null-makes-it-nullable.description: A value seen as null too may be null, and keeps its description.

null-first.description: The same with null seen first.

null-and-an-array.description: An array seen as null too may be null, and keeps its items, without an example: no element was seen as null.

null-then-an-array.description: The same with null seen first: a takes the array.

null-in-a-tuple-position.description: The same one level deeper, in a position of a tuple, as OpenSky's state vector has.

null-then-an-empty-array.description: An array seen as null and only ever empty.

empty-then-with-items.description: An array seen empty, then with items, takes the items and drops the bound.

with-items-then-empty.description: The same the other way round.

always-empty.description: An array only ever seen empty keeps maxItems 0.

bounds-widen.description: minItems and maxItems widen to hold both.

tuple-positions-merge.description: Tuples of one length merge position by position.

tuple-positions-that-differ.description: A position that cannot merge is reported where it is.

tuple-and-list.description: A tuple and a list cannot line up, so both are alternatives.

list-fitting-a-tuple.description: Pixellab's 3D keypoint: a recorded [x, y, z] is inferred as a list of numbers, as it keeps no length, and fits every position of the tuple.

lists-go-to-the-list.description: Each further list goes to the list, rather than nesting a union around the tuple every time.

tuple-of-another-length.description: A tuple of another length is an alternative of its own.

infinity-stays-a-number.description: A value that overflowed to "Infinity", recorded as a string, keeps a's number type.

infinity-takes-the-number.description: The same the other way round: b's number wins.

zero-double-stays-a-string.description: A value recorded as exactly 0.0 says no more than that, so a keeps its string type.

date-time-or-timestamp.description: A date seen as a date-time string and as a unix timestamp is a oneOf of both.

timestamp-or-date-time.description: The same with the timestamp first.

date-as-integer.description: An integer with format date, merged with a plain integer.

date-or-date-time.description: A date and a date-time are alternatives of their own, and further samples of either go to theirs.

date-time-or-date.description: The same with the date-time first.

date-time-into-the-oneof.description: A date-time merged into the oneOf goes to its alternative.

oneof-on-b.description: With the oneOf on b, the result is still a.

title-and-description-survive.description: a's title and description stay when b's oneOf becomes the result.

nothing-into-the-oneof.description: A schema saying nothing changes nothing, as merging the same samples again would.

nothing-with-the-oneof-on-b.description: The same with the oneOf on b.

null-into-the-oneof.description: A null makes the oneOf nullable.

oneof-into-oneof.description: Two oneOfs of the same alternatives merge alternative by alternative.

oneof-into-itself.description: Merging a oneOf into itself, as enriching twice over the same data does, changes nothing.

null-alternative-in-b.description: A null alternative of b's makes the result nullable, and the others go to theirs.

property-keeps-its-place.description: A property that becomes a oneOf keeps its place.

items-of-different-objects.description: Array items that are objects of different shapes.

rich-text-of-another-type.description: Notion's rich text, seen as text and as a mention.

allof-part-declaring-the-property.description: A property goes to the allOf part that declares it.

only-what-both-require.description: A value without a member makes it optional; one b requires but a does not stays optional.

alternative-declaring-the-member.description: Notion's filter forms pin nothing: the one declaring the sample's member takes it, not the first.

fuller-alternative-made-optional.description: Notion's database lacks database_type, which the full form requires: it is still the full form, which no longer requires it.

required-in-allof-parts.description: Split among an allOf's parts, a sample narrows each part only by what it leaves out.

additional-properties-both-absent.description: additionalProperties absent on both stays absent.

additional-properties-absent-and-false.description: Absent says nothing, so false stays.

additional-properties-true-and-absent.description: The same the other way round, with true.

additional-properties-true-and-false.description: The same the other way round.

additional-properties-schema-and-true.description: The same the other way round.

map-values-in-order.description: The values of a map merge in the order they were recorded, so the value schema keeps the first example, every time.

samples-into-their-alternatives.description: Merged as one, the two samples would hold both members and match neither alternative; each goes to the one it matches.

samples-into-no-union.description: Into a schema that is no union, each sample is merged in turn.

samples-join-samples.description: Samples are no alternatives to route among: more of them join the union, for the caller to collapse.

union-by-pinned-value.description: A value goes to the alternative whose pinned member it has, and the other keeps its own.

union-in-allof.description: Of an allOf of a common part and a union, the part takes what it declares, the alternative what no part does.

anyof-of-unions.description: An anyOf of unions routes to the alternative inside; a reference to a reference stands for what the last refers to.

integer-into-number.description: An integer is a number, so it goes to the number alternative.

uri-into-string.description: A string without a format takes any.

no-alternative-matches.description: A value no alternative pins fails.

anyof-on-b.description: A sample routes the same with the union on b, and the result is the union.

anyof-into-union.description: An anyOf merged into a union merges each of its alternatives.

full-beats-partial.description: A partial object pins what the full one does, so the one declaring more of what was recorded takes it.

no-alternative-of-the-type.description: A type no alternative has fails.

no-alternative-of-the-type-on-b.description: The same with the oneOf on b.

alternative-of-b-matching-none.description: b's alternative that matches none of a's fails, at its index.

types-that-differ.description: Types that cannot be reconciled fail, showing both schemas.
